about: Past macro-event dates the pre-market brief uses as historical analogues. Compiled from the public schedules (RBI MPC resolutions, Union Budget days, Lok Sabha exit-poll and result days, US FOMC statements); the FY25 and FY26 RBI dates were checked against RBI's announced schedules on 3 Nov 2026, the rest are not yet checked line by line. A wrong date dilutes an analogue; it cannot reach a trade (the brief places nothing). Add new dates as they pass.

rbi.label: RBI MPC decision
rbi.evidence: Exploratory, NIFTY and BANKNIFTY 2019-2026 bhavcopy (3 Nov 2026): on RBI days that were not expiry days, a near-money liquid option closed at 3x its open on 17.5% of sessions against 12.5% on other non-expiry sessions (57 sessions; not significant). Not a tested rule.

fomc.label: US FOMC decision
fomc.evidence: Exploratory (3 Nov 2026): the Indian session after an FOMC decision showed twice the usual 3x-spike rate only because it was usually a Thursday expiry; on mornings that were not expiry days the rate was 3%, below the usual 12.5% (33 sessions). Not a spike signal.

budget.label: Union Budget
budget.evidence: Exploratory (3 Nov 2026): 13 budget sessions since 2019, too few to say anything about spikes.

election.label: General election (exit polls, results)
election.evidence: Exploratory (3 Nov 2026): the four exit-poll and result sessions of 2019 and 2024 are the biggest spike days in the record (non-expiry: a near-money option at 3x on half of them). Rare: twice a decade.
